query: High-yield isolation of pancreatic islets from adult mice using collagenase digestion and density-gradient purification
title: A Simple High Efficiency Protocol for Pancreatic Islet Isolation from Mice
markdown:
## Protocol: High-yield isolation of pancreatic islets from adult mice using collagenase digestion and density-gradient purification

### Overview

This protocol details the high-yield isolation of pancreatic islets from adult mice using collagenase P digestion via intraductal injection, followed by density-gradient purification. The procedure encompasses reagent preparation, surgical isolation, enzymatic digestion, centrifugation steps, and final culture or storage of isolated islets.

### Materials/Reagents

Hank's Balanced Salt Solution (HBSS) (1X and 10X stock), Fetal Bovine Serum (FBS) (100X stock), Collagenase P, Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA), RPMI 1640 Medium (with 5.5 mM glucose), Penicillin (100 U/mL), Streptomycin (100 μg/mL), INS-1 Cell Supplement (10 mM HEPES, 2 mM L-glutamine, 1 mM sodium pyruvate, 0.05 mM 2-mercaptoethanol), Isoflurane, RNase Inhibiting Solution, 70% Ethanol, Distilled Water.

### Equipment

Syringes (3 mL), Needles (30 G ½ in), Schwartz micro serrefines, Micro Adson forceps, Curved surgical scissors, Cover glass forceps, Dissection microscope, Centrifuge (swinging-bucket), Water bath (37 °C), Incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2, 95% humidity), 50 mL tubes, 100 mm Petri dishes, 1.5 mL tubes, Absorbent pads (6 in x 6 in).

### Safety & Sterility

All tools must be soaked in RNase inhibiting solution for 30 min prior to use, then cleaned with 70% ethanol and distilled water, and air-dried on clean paper towels to eliminate potential RNases. Maintain sterile conditions during surgery and islet handling. Euthanize mice via cervical dislocation after deep anesthesia confirmation.

## Reagent Preparation

### Preparation

1. Prepare Hank's Balanced Salt Solution (HBSS) by adding 100 mL of 10X HBSS stock to 900 mL of distilled water to make 1 L of 1X HBSS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
2. Prepare STOP solution by adding 50 mL of 100X fetal bovine serum (FBS) to 450 mL of ice-cold 1X HBSS to make 500 mL of STOP solution; keep at 4 °C and use within 1 h of preparation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->
3. Prepare collagenase P solution by adding 1 mg/mL of collagenase P to ice-cold 1X HBSS (use 6 mL per mouse); add 0.05% (w/v) bovine serum albumin (BSA) (e.g., 3 mg BSA in 6 mL solution) to provide nutrients; keep on ice and prepare fresh within 1 h of use; calculate total volume needed for all mice into one 50 mL tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S03 -->
4. Prepare complete RPMI 1640 medium by adding 10% FBS, 100 U/mL penicillin, 100 μg/mL streptomycin, and INS-1 cell supplement (10 mM HEPES, 2 mM L-glutamine, 1 mM sodium pyruvate, and 0.05 mM 2-mercaptoethanol) to 500 mL of RPMI 1640 media containing 5.5 mM glucose for overnight culture. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S04 -->
5. Fill three 50 mL tubes of 25 mL RNase inhibiting solution, 70% ethanol or distilled H _2 O. These solutions will be used for cleaning surgical tools prior and during the procedure. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S05 -->
6. Soak the tips of all tools in RNase inhibiting solution for 30 min before starting the protocol to eliminate potential RNases. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S06 -->
7. Pre-cut absorbent pads to 6 in x 6 in size for use during surgery. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S07 -->
8. Prepare 1X HBSS solution in advance and store at 4 °C; prepare STOP solution prior to surgery and store at 4 °C. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S08 -->
9. Prepare collagenase P solution immediately prior to surgery and store on ice; note that it should be used within 2 h of preparation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S09 -->
10. Label 50 mL tubes for digestion and purification; prepare two tubes per mouse (one for digestion, one for purification) and ensure the animal ID is marked on both. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S10 -->
11. Add 3 mL of collagenase P solution into the first 50 mL digestion tube; reserve the remaining 3 mL for injection. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S11 -->
12. Draw the remaining 3 mL of collagenase P solution into a 3 mL syringe mounted with a 30 G ½ in needle and place the syringe on ice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S12 -->

## Surgical Isolation and Digestion

### Surgery Start

1. Remove all tools from RNase inhibiting solution, dip them first in 70% ethanol, then in distilled water, and air-dry on a clean paper towel. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->
2. Place the mouse in a chamber containing 0.5 mL of isoflurane until deeply anesthetized. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->
3. Remove the mouse from the chamber and confirm deep anesthesia by pinching a foot pad with forceps; deep anesthesia is indicated by steadily slow breathing and lack of reaction to pinching. Euthanize the mouse via cervical dislocation (apply pressure to the neck and pull the tail to dislocate the spinal column) and place the mouse on an absorbent pad. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S03 -->
4. Tape the limbs of the mouse in a supine position to the absorbent pad, spray the body with 70% ethanol, and wipe off excess ethanol. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S04 -->
5. Using cover glass forceps and curved surgical scissors, make a horizontal incision (~3 cm) on the abdominal skin, pull the skin wide open to expose the abdominal wall, then make a vertical incision (~3-4 cm) on the abdominal peritoneum to fully expose the pancreas. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S05 -->
6. Push the liver lobes superiorly to expose the bile duct, which appears as a pale pink tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S06 -->
7. Carefully move the intestines from the right lumbar/iliac region to the right to expose the bile duct and hepatic artery. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S07 -->
8. Carefully clamp the common bile duct using Schwartz micro serrefines as close to the liver as possible. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S08 -->
9. Identify the ampulla of Vater at the duodenal papilla (formed by the union of the pancreatic duct and common bile duct); it appears swollen under a dissection microscope and serves as the entry point to the common bile duct. Adjusting the light intensity/angle may aid location. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S09 -->
10. Insert the syringe containing 3 mL of collagenase P solution into the ampulla of Vater; push the needle into the duct for about 1/4 of the length of the common bile duct. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S10 -->
11. Once the needle is in the ampulla, ensure its orientation is parallel with the duct. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S11 -->
12. Stabilize the needle by clamping it with micro Adson forceps to prevent puncturing the duct. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S12 -->
13. Slowly and steadily inject 3 mL of collagenase P solution into the common bile duct until resistance is felt; the goal is to create backflow pressure to force collagenase into the pancreatic duct. Success is confirmed if the head, neck, body, and tail regions of the pancreas are fully inflated. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S13 -->
14. Carefully dissect out the inflated pancreas using two forceps (curved and Micro Adson), starting from the spleen and pulling away from the spleen, stomach, and along the duodenum; place the pancreas into a 50 mL digestion tube containing 3 mL of ice-cold collagenase P solution. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S14 -->
15. Chop the pancreas for 3-5 s in the digestion tube with 3 mL of ice-cold collagenase P solution using fine surgical scissors; no additional incisions are required. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S15 -->

### Digestion Incubation

1. Secure the tube to a rack in a 37 °C water bath and shake at 100-120 rpm for approximately 12-13 min. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S01 -->
2. After incubation, gently shake the tube by hand for about 30 s to disrupt tissue until the solution becomes homogenous with a sand-like appearance of fine pancreas particles; hold the tube up to light to check homogeneity and shake for another ~15 s if needed. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S02 -->
3. Immediately place the tubes on ice and add 40 mL of ice-cold STOP solution to terminate enzymatic digestion. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S03 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note: Digestion tubes can remain on ice for up to 2 h if processing multiple mice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S04 -->

### Centrifugation and Washing

1. Centrifuge the tube in a swinging-bucket centrifuge at 300 x g for 30 s (temperature is flexible). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note: Use a swinging-bucket centrifuge to ensure the tissue pellet forms at the bottom of the 50 mL tube, not on the wall, which is critical for better islet yield. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S02 -->
2. Decant the supernatant and repeat centrifugation with STOP solution two more times, decanting after each spin; use 20 mL of STOP solution for each subsequent wash. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S03 -->
3. Before each spin, disrupt the pellet by gently shaking the tissue pellet in the 50 mL tube containing 20 mL of STOP solution. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S04 -->
4. Re-suspend the tissue pellet with 40 mL of ice-cold HBSS and centrifuge at 300 x g for 30 s. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S05 -->
5. Decant the supernatant and repeat centrifugation using a swinging-bucket centrifuge with HBSS solution two more times, decanting after each spin; use 20 mL of HBSS for each wash. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S06 -->
6. Before each spin, disrupt the pellet to detach it from the bottom of the tube by gently shaking the tube containing 20 mL of HBSS solution. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S07 -->
7. After the last centrifugation, remove all HBSS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T2-S08 -->

### Density Gradient Purification

1. Add 5 mL of room temperature density gradient to the 50 mL tube containing the pellet and vortex briefly at low speed until homogenized. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S01 -->
2. Add another 5 mL of room temperature density gradient to the 50 mL tube; do not vortex or mix. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S02 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note: It is critical to remain steady and still to allow the gradient to form without disruption. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S03 -->
3. Pipette 10 mL of room temperature HBSS buffer into the tube drop-by-drop gently and slowly to allow a gradient to form; use a pipette gun with a 10 mL pipette. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S04 -->
4. Spin tubes in a swinging-bucket centrifuge at 1700 x g for 15 min; set acceleration/deceleration speeds to the lowest setting to maintain the gradient. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S05 -->
5. After spinning, carefully remove tubes without disturbing the gradient; using a pipette gun pre-wetted with cold HBSS, pipette out the layer of islets (5-10 mL) formed between the density gradient and HBSS into a new 50 mL islet collection tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S06 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note: Wetting the pipette with cold HBSS prior to pipetting helps prevent islets from sticking to the inner walls of the pipette. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S07 -->
6. If separation is incomplete and islets are visible in the density gradient layer, pipette out the entire 10 mL of the density gradient (bottom layer) along with the islet layer at the interface, leaving only about 8-10 mL of the HBSS top layer behind. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S08 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note: Collecting both the islet layer and the density gradient layer may collect debris and lengthen picking time but does not alter other steps; this is unnecessary when the islet layer is well-formed. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T3-S09 -->

### Final Washing

1. Add 20 mL of ice-cold HBSS to the new 50 mL tube containing islets and centrifuge at 350 x g for 3 min in a swinging-bucket centrifuge. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S01 -->
2. After spinning, carefully pipette out the supernatant (do not decant), leaving ~3 mL at the bottom without disturbing the islet pellet; discard the supernatant. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S02 -->
3. Repeat washing and centrifuging at least 3 times, adding 20 mL of HBSS each time and suspending the pellet before each spin. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T4-S03 -->

### Islet Recovery and Culture

1. Warm the RPMI-1640 complete media bottle in a 37 °C water bath prior to use. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S01 -->
2. After the last centrifugation, remove all HBSS and add 4 mL of previously prepared complete RPMI-1640 media (containing FBS, INS-1 cell supplement, and penicillin/streptomycin) to the pellet. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S02 -->
3. Dislodge the pellet by gently swirling the tube and pour the media into a 100 mm Petri dish; add another 5 mL of RPMI-1640 media to the tube, swirl gently to wash off remaining islets, and pour into the same Petri dish. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S03 -->
4. Under a dissection microscope, pick healthy islets using a 20 μL pipette and transfer them to a new Petri dish containing 10 mL of complete RPMI 1640 media; healthy islets appear spherical/oblong, golden-brown, and smooth, unlike transparent, wispy exocrine tissue. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S04 -->
5. Incubate islets in a sterile incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO2 and 95% humidified air overnight for next-day experiments, or freeze for later analysis. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S06 -->
6. To freeze cells, place islets in HBSS buffer, collect in 200-500 μL of buffer, transfer to a 1.5 mL tube, centrifuge at 350 x g for 1-2 min, remove supernatant leaving no more than 30-40 μL, and store at -20 °C (short term, several days) or -80 °C (long term). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T5-S07 -->
